headlines: Telecoms sharply lower: T -7.4%, VZ -6.3% on heavy volume, cause not found; ASTS -8% and SPCX flat/red mentioned by posters linking a satellite-to-phone threat
No major US economic releases today; Canada unemployment 6.5% vs 6.4%
Posters flag DAL and PEP guidance weakness and say ~40% of S&P stocks are in bear markets

rumors.text: Posters link the T/VZ/TMUS selloff to satellite direct-to-phone competition (SPCX/ASTS); others call it overdone and note fiber is unaffected
rumors.why: If satellite carriers threaten wireless spectrum value, legacy telecoms keep falling

rumors.text: Posters say about 40% of S&P stocks are in bear markets and companies like DAL and PEP are pulling guidance, risking an earnings-growth reset into year end
rumors.why: Weak guidance would hit index earnings expectations and narrow breadth

rumors.text: Fed officials Waller and Musalem reportedly signaled more rate hikes (carried from last hour, not re-confirmed)
rumors.why: More hikes would pressure valuations and long bonds

rumors.text: Posters see SPY pinned near 775 with a quiet no-news Friday and chop around VWAP
rumors.why: Range-bound action limits downside absent headlines

plays.reason: SPY has turned green (+0.28%) with QQQ and IWM up; no scheduled catalysts and a quiet Friday tape, while Fed-hike talk and weak breadth cap the edge
plays.catalyst: Quiet Friday drift, chip rebound holding

readings.whats_new: SPY flipped from -0.17% to +0.28% (776.07) and QQQ from -0.76% to +0.24% as the chip rebound held. Telecoms are now the standout loser (T -7.4%, VZ -6.3%) on heavy volume with a possible satellite-competition angle but no confirmed cause. Fear and greed is steady near 38 and VIX is flat at 15.15; no US data is due today.
